1. Mr. T.P.S. Takuli, learned counsel for the
petitioner.
2. Mr. Amarendra Pratap Singh, learned Additional
Advocate General for the State of Uttarakhand/
respondent no. 1.
3. Mr. Pankaj Miglani, learned counsel for
respondent no. 2.
4. Petitioner, who belongs to Scheduled Tribe,
participated in a selection for appointment to the post
of Veterinary Medical Officer, Grade-2 held pursuant to
an advertisement issued by Uttarakhand Public Service
Commission. Petitioner was not recommended for
appointment, while respondent nos. 3 & 4 were
selected and recommended for appointment.
5. I n this Writ Petition, petitioner has challenged
selection and appointment of respondent nos. 3 & 4, on
the ground that the petitioner possessed Masters
Degree in Veterinary Science, which is preferential
qualification, and he was also having experience of
serving as a Veterinary Doctor in Nainital Dugdh
Utpadak Sangh Samiti, therefore, he had a better claim
for appointment.
6. Mr. Pankaj Miglani, learned counsel for
Uttarakhand Public Service Commission points out that
the last selected candidate in Scheduled Tribe category
scored 55% marks, while petitioner could score only
35% marks, therefore, petitioner could not be

recommended for appointment. He further subm its
that, although the advertisement mentions that
preference shall be given to Post Graduate degree
holders, however, petitioner was entitled to preference,
only if his score of marks was equal to the last selected
candidate in the Scheduled Tribe category. Thus, he
submits that the Writ Petition is devoid of merits. He
points out that fresh selection process for appointment
to the post of Veterinary Medical Officer is initiated by
issuing advertisement on 12.10.2023.
7. Since selection is merit based, and merit is
evaluated based on marks scored by a candidate in the
written examination/ viva- voce, therefore, no direction
can be issued to appoint the petitioner, who,
admittedly, has scored less marks than the candidates
recommended for appointment against vacancies
reserved for Scheduled Tribe category. Preferential
qualification becom es relevant when all other things
between two candidates are equal, then one with
preferential qualification is appointed. Since this is not
the case here, therefore, there is no force in the claim
made by petitioner.
8. Accordingly, the Writ Petition fails, and is
dism issed. No order as to costs.
9. Consequently, pending application(s), if any, also
stand disposed of.
